sentimentIssues: 26 tickerSentiment rows for 8 names (ELF x8, HIMS x7, AMZN x5). Unusable as a table.
ELF gets contradictory rows at 152s (neutral/hold and bullish/long).
The CELH 'hold' stance is fine. META 'long' is OK, but it is a realized-gain brag, not a current call.
SoFi 'bullish/long' is defensible ('we're going to see the appreciation very soon').
why: Both find the same three ideas with the same targets. LeapEdge delivers them as three clean, ticker-resolved trade cards with target, horizon, catalysts and risks: HIMS $100 in 3-7y, AMZN $300+ by year-end or early next year, ELF $400 in 3-7y. Ours has more supporting detail (ELF penetration, HIMS facilities, CELH/META/SOFI) but leaves AMZN and ELF with null tickers and puts targets only in prose. It also splits each idea into two calls, emits 26 sentiment rows and ends with 12 pipeline-noise omissions. A PM skimming this would act faster on LeapEdge.
recommendations: Add structured target/horizon fields to calls and fill them: 'AMZN target $300+, horizon: before YE or early next year, trigger: capex slowdown announcement'. Today the $300 lives only inside thesis text.
Merge calls per ticker. The ELF 're-entered, undervalued' call and the 'ELF $400 in 3-7y' call are one idea; keep the target-bearing one and fold the rest into the rationale.
Resolve tickers. 'ELF' spoken literally still got ticker null. A symbol dictionary plus an exact-match pass on spoken uppercase tokens would fix AMZN/ELF/CELH/META/SOFI/NOW.
Add valuation snapshot fields when the creator reads them out (AMZN TTM P/E 20.79, fwd 24.09, 52w 196-287; ELF fwd P/E 28.59). Ours dropped the AMZN numbers entirely.
Capture macro context the creator ties to the calls (oil -9% w/w, 'oil down -> ELF up', skepticism on Trump/Iran headlines).
Delete generic 'analyst wish-list' omissions ('off-balance sheet lease commitments for Amazon') and all source-N / sN pipeline lines from the user-facing brief.
